findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plain text in the Lambda function's environment variables and committed to source control. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or repository read access can retrieve these long-lived static credentials.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so environment variables (which contain secrets here) are encrypted only with the default service-owned Lambda key, giving no control over key policy, rotation, or access auditing.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.
No code_signing_config_arn is attached, so the deployment package is not signature-verified; tampering with the zip artefact between build and deployment would go undetected.
